items.title: D'Imperio interviewed by Monk Rowe, 2014
items.q: Now the band director that came in to the New York Army Band replaced a marching band director and the new director was named Mr. Shettle S-H-E-T-T-L-E.

ctx.x: No — yes, this was a concert band. We played parades up and down Fifth Avenue, you know, the whole bit. But then there’d be the symphonic band, I mean the concert band, and I was good a tympani because that’s what I played in high school, because of my ear, and I could tune and play the tympani and all that. So I wound up playing — so in other words all the guys in the percussion are saying they’re supposed to alternate playing with what they call the stage band then, you know, the New York Army Stage Band, which…

music not balls to the walls bluster. So he decided to get everybody a thing where the government paid for lessons. Well you could pick your own teacher. And I went up to Henry and I sought Sonny downstairs, and I said, “man, I’d really like to study with you.” And I said, “I’ve been on the road with the Salt City Six” and this and that, “and I’m in the New York Army Band.” And he wasn’t being facetious I don’t think, but he knew me and — we’re not friends yet, but when I said I’d been on the road with the Salt…
